title: Summer temperature and water balance gave no clear change in the autumn-to-spring nocturnal bird passage ratio at 11-18 European weather radars in 2014-2024 after quality control
abstract: Question: do warm or dry summers (May-July) decrease the ratio of autumn to spring nocturnal bird passage measured by weather radar, an observer-free index of breeding output? Data: BALTRAD vertical profile time series (Aloft repository, CC0) for 25 radars in 8 European countries, March-May and August-October 2014-2024 (1,184 monthly files), and CRU TS 4.09 temperature and P-PET. Method: nightly migration traffic from sunset to sunrise, season totals, R = ln(autumn/spring) per radar-year (calibration constant within a year cancels), radar and year fixed effects, radar-cluster bootstrap. Result: quality control is the main constraint. Of 198 radar-years, 100 kept one processing regime in all six months and only 62 also had valid ground-speed retrieval. In the clean sample (47 radar-years, 11 radars with 3 or more clean years) a 1 SD warmer summer (0.81 C) changed R by -0.19 (95% CI -0.56 to +0.31) and a 1 SD wetter summer (+50 mm) by -0.07 (CI -0.33 to +0.31). A temperature-only model gave -0.13 (CI -0.31 to -0.01), but this slope was not robust (-0.10, CI -0.19 to +0.01, with 18 radars). The pre-specified model (96 radar-years) gave larger negative slopes with wide intervals; inspection showed that months without ground-speed retrieval produced ratios up to e^8, so we added a speed rule and report both. Spring and autumn passage dates had no clear temperature link. Limitations: small clean sample, very few southern radars, no 2018-2019 or 2022 data passed QC, one climate box per radar. Code, nightly traffic for all 25 radars, QC tables and a regeneration script are included.
